In the Intel 8085A microprocessor, every instruction begins with fetching the opcode from memory.  
This first machine cycle is specifically called the **op-code fetch cycle**, identified by the IO/M‾ signal being low and S1 and S0 both high.  
Other machine cycles (memory read, memory write, I/O read, I/O write) may follow depending on the instruction, but the first one is always the op-code fetch.  

Final answer: (A)
